Where it began

Devdutt Padikkal was born in Edappal, Kerala, on 7 July 2000. The family were living in Hyderabad, but his father decided that Bengaluru was the place for a young cricketer to grow, and at ten Devdutt joined the Karnataka Institute of Cricket there.

He went to the Army Public School and St Joseph's Boys' High School in Bengaluru, and later took a business degree at St Joseph's College of Commerce. Not many top-order batters can read a balance sheet as well as a scoreboard.

The player

He first played for Karnataka in November 2018, and his first one-day season brought 609 runs in eleven matches, more than anyone else in the Vijay Hazare Trophy. A first-class hundred, 178 against Puducherry, followed in 2022.

India first picked him for a T20 international against Sri Lanka in July 2021. His Test chance came in March 2024, when he was called up during the England series and played the fifth Test, making 65 in his first innings. In August 2026 he made his first Test hundred, 167 against Sri Lanka, and in the very next Test, at Colombo, he made 117. By November 2026 he had played four Tests and scored 418 runs at 69.67.

What made him special

He is a left-hander who bats at the top of the order and who likes a long innings once he is in: his two Test hundreds took 230 and 193 balls. He made an early name in the IPL with Royal Challengers Bengaluru, where nobody before him had made three fifties in his first four games. He was the league's Emerging Player in 2020 and made an unbeaten 101 the next year as Bengaluru won by ten wickets.

His bowling is another matter. By November 2026 he had bowled in Tests without taking a wicket, though with an average like his, India were happy to leave the ball in other hands.

Away from the middle

After spells with Rajasthan Royals and Lucknow Super Giants, he went back to Royal Challengers Bengaluru for the 2025 season. In April 2022, playing for Rajasthan, he passed 1,000 IPL runs.

And finally

By November 2026 his Test average sat at 69.67. Few batters begin a Test career that way, and he will be in no hurry to see it come down.
